_comment: ATLAS v7.0 — declarative cleanup rules. Read by hooks/cleanup-runner.js each SessionStart. Paths are relative to CLAUDE_DIR. Ordering is preserved. Add a rule here instead of a new session-start.sh section.

rules.name: version-manifest-nag
rules.description: VERSION-MANIFEST staleness nag (was §7a)

rules.name: tool-health-prune
rules.description: Keep last 20 failure timestamps per tool (was §7a2)

rules.name: trash-prune
rules.description: Expire items in TRASH after 3 days (was §7a2)

rules.name: session-cache-prune
rules.description: Per-project session UUID-dir rotation (was §7a3)

rules.name: python-cache
rules.description: Remove Python __pycache__ under hooks/ (was §7b)

rules.name: debug-cleanup
rules.description: Debug .txt files older than 14 days (was §7c)
rules._note: Verified-dead target as of 2026-06-15 (deep audit): no native or ATLAS writer of ~/.claude/debug/ exists (project-local .flow/debug is the only debug dir created). Harmless ~0ms no-op each session; retained defensively, symmetric with other guard rules. Do NOT confuse with stale-todos — ~/.claude/todos/ IS a live lazily-created dir (native TodoWrite); that rule must stay.

rules.name: shell-snapshots
rules.description: Shell snapshots: age-prune 14d and cap at 50 (was §7d)

rules.name: stale-todos
rules.description: Stale todo .json files older than 3 days (was §7e)

rules.name: plans-rotation
rules.description: v8.14: repointed at plans/archive/ (cap 40). Live plans/ is owned by session-stop.sh §5, which ARCHIVES all but the 5 newest (+ <!-- keep --> exemptions) — the old delete-based keep-15 on plans/ was dead in practice and would have DELETED plans if the stop hook ever missed

rules.name: session-env-rotation
rules.description: Session-env subdirs older than 7 days (was §7g)

rules.name: cache-efficiency
rules.description: Keep last 10 cache efficiency snapshots (was §7h)

rules.name: session-reminders-prune
rules.description: Keep last 10 per-session reminder flag files (added 2026-05-28 / jazzy-wren audit — accumulated unmanaged, one per session)

rules.name: context-mode-stats-prune
rules.description: Expire per-PID context-mode stats files after 14 days; content/*.db (live DB) is untouched (added 2026-06-24 / system audit — 381 files had accumulated unmanaged)

rules.name: transcripts-rotation
rules.description: Gzip >1MB+7d transcripts; trash .gz >30d (was §7j)

rules.name: plugin-skill-pack-nag
rules.description: Plugin skill-pack freshness weekly nag (was §7k)

rules.name: log-rotation-chatty
rules.description: Rotate chatty logs at 500KB (local-llm-reads, tool-failures, action-graph-stats, hook-health) — prevent unbounded growth (added 2026-05-15 / audit)

rules.name: log-bak-prune
rules.description: Expire rotated .bak log files after 30 days (added 2026-05-15 / audit)

rules.name: active-system-prune
rules.description: Capability-system activation markers + digests idle >14d (sliding TTL — session-start §7m touches them on every session in that CWD; added v8.6.0)

rules.name: system-detect-prune
rules.description: system-detect.js per-CWD proposal throttle files >48h (added v8.6.0)

rules.name: knowledge-view-prune
rules.description: Generated per-domain knowledge views (regenerated on /system activate; added v8.6.0)

rules.name: dated-handoffs-prune
rules.description: Dated per-session handoffs (handoffs/<slug>/<ts>.md, written by session-handoff.js at SessionEnd) expire after 30d — they had NO pruner and grew unbounded; depth 2 also covers the depth-1 per-CWD snapshots (harmless overlap with session-start §1's 14d prune). Added v8.14.0 audit

rules.name: ide-lock-prune
rules.description: Stale IDE-bridge lock files (pid+authToken per VS Code window); live extensions rewrite their lock on reconnect, so >14d mtime = dead process (added v8.14.0 audit — 8 had accumulated since May)

rules.name: stale-task-lists
rules.description: Native per-session task-list dirs (tasks/<session-uuid>/N.json); dir mtime = last task write. 30d > the 14d session rotation, so no resumable session loses its list (added v8.14.0 audit — 9 had accumulated unmanaged)

rules.name: global-trash-prune
rules.description: Expire items in the global bash_hook.py trash (C:/tmp/trash/<name>-<epoch>) after 14 days — closes the 'cleanup engine clears trash on schedule' promise, which previously only covered ~/.claude/TRASH (added v8.14.0 audit). match_all expires dir-shaped items via rmRf like the TRASH rule; trashed transcripts live in the sibling C:/tmp/claude-transcripts-trash precisely so this rule cannot rmRf them early

rules.name: trashed-transcripts-prune
rules.description: Expire trashed session-transcript .jsonl.gz 30d after they land (they already survived 30d live + gzip stage). Added v8.14.0 audit alongside the trash_dir POSIX→Windows path fix that had been silently diverting these to C:\c\tmp since the v7.0 bash→Node port (107MB migrated). Sibling of C:/tmp/trash so global-trash-prune's match_all dir-expiry can't collide
